newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: HEINEKEN TO STAY IN ZAIRE AFTER BREWERY PLUNDERED.
newsitem.headline: HEINEKEN TO STAY IN ZAIRE AFTER BREWERY PLUNDERED.

text.p: Dutch brewing giant Heineken NV said on Monday it remained committed to operating in Zaire, despite the destruction of its brewery at Bukavu in eastern Zaire over the weekend.

"Heineken will not pull out of the region," said Heineken spokesman Koos Woltjes, restating the company's position since fighting spilled into the region and expressing regret at news that a security guard had died after an attack on the brewery.
Heineken, which has operated in central Africa for 50 years, had shut the 400,000 hectolitre-per-year capacity brewery after clashes between Zairean troops and Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels.
Woltjes said closing down operations in the region would have only a minor impact on the group's overall profits.

The company had been in contact with Zaire this morning, he said, and things had not worsened since the weekend. He said Heineken might decide whether expatriate employees and their families would be evacuated, but not necessarily today.
At the moment, the families of the expatriate employees in Zaire can opt for evacuation. Heineken employs some 12 expatriates in Zaire.
